claim: The paper's finding that the largest models it tests need only about two components to reproduce a prediction is not established, because each reported size is a median taken only over the predictions on which the paper's search for a sufficient set of components succeeded, and that search fails on a large share of the predictions of exactly those large models.
evidence: Table 40 (Section 6.3) gives, per model, how many of the sampled predictions the search verified, and its caption states that "the size and the controls are over those"; the text adds that the remaining predictions are "excluded from everything to its right." The verified counts are 32 of 60 predictions for Qwen2.5 7B, 47 of 60 for Mistral 7B, 65 of 150 for Qwen2.5 1.5B and 60 of 150 for Llama-3.2 1B, against 131 of 150 for GPT-2 124M and 141 of 150 for OPT 125M. On the predictions where the search fails, the set is not small: on the paper's own baseline, Section 2.5 reports that "where the repair never converges it has already built a mean of 489 components, at most 962 or two percent of the model, and the token still does not come out." The abstract nevertheless states that "the sufficient set runs from two components to sixteen", and Section 6.3 that "the largest models sit at its small end: Mistral 7B and Qwen2.5 7B rest on two components each", although for Qwen2.5 7B almost half of the sampled predictions (28 of 60) have no sufficient set found at all.
